widgetMetadata.instructions: Each entry under `widgets` describes one chart/widget rendered on this page of the Israeli Ecosystem dashboard. Descriptions are result-agnostic: they explain what the visualization shows and how to interpret it, not the specific numbers. The `dataPaths` array on each entry lists dot-notation paths inside this same JSON file where the underlying data for that widget lives (e.g. "kpis.patentingStartups" or "ipIntensity.items") When summarizing or answering questions about a number from this snapshot, locate the relevant widget(s) by `dataPaths` and quote the corresponding `description` to explain the metric. Widgets that have a 10 year trend usually show the total overall (across all years) and you get the exact data for each year in the past 10 years. The 10 year data do not add up to the total of course

startups:map.title: Israel Startup Map
startups:map.description: Geographic distribution of Israeli startups by their registered address in Israel. Each city marker is sized by the number of startups with an active legal registration in that city and colored by its administrative district. The legend lists the same totals by district. Only startups with a known registered Israeli address appear.

startups:kpi-total-startups.title: Total Startups
startups:kpi-total-startups.description: Total number of Israeli startups in the dataset (active, exited, and closed combined). The bar chart shows new startups by founding year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-funding-rounds.title: Funding Rounds
startups:kpi-funding-rounds.description: Total number of equity rounds raised by Israeli startups across all time: money paid into the company for newly issued shares, from pre-seed through late stage, including SAFEs, convertible notes and bridges. The bar chart shows the count of rounds closed each year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-total-raised.title: Total Raised
startups:kpi-total-raised.description: Total capital (USD) Israeli startups raised in equity rounds: money paid into the company for newly issued shares, from pre-seed through late stage, including SAFEs, convertible notes and bridges. The bar chart shows the dollar amount raised each year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-acquisitions.title: Acquisitions
startups:kpi-acquisitions.description: Total number of Israeli startups that exited via a completed acquisition, meaning a deal that actually went ahead. The bar chart shows acquisitions by exit year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-ipos.title: IPOs
startups:kpi-ipos.description: Total number of Israeli startups that exited via IPO and reached the market, meaning shares priced or trading on a public exchange. The bar chart shows IPOs by exit year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-time-to-exit.title: Time to Exit
startups:kpi-time-to-exit.description: Average number of years between founding year and exit year (acquisition or IPO) across all exited Israeli startups. The histogram shows the distribution of those exit times in 1-year buckets, capped at 30+ years.

startups:survival-distribution.title: Survival Distribution
startups:survival-distribution.description: Breakdown of all Israeli startups by current status: Active (still operating), Closed (shut down or dissolved), and Exit (acquired or went public). The center of the donut shows the total number of startups, or the value of the hovered slice.

startups:exit-funnel.title: Exit Funnel
startups:exit-funnel.description: How many Israeli startups make it through each progressive milestone toward an exit: All startups (everyone in the dataset), Funded (raised at least one equity round), $1M+ (raised at least $1 million in total), $10M+ (raised at least $10 million in total), Exit (a completed acquisition or public listing). The percentage on each segment is the retention from the All-startups stage.

startups:time-to-exit.title: Time To Exit
startups:time-to-exit.description: Average and median number of years between founding year and exit year (acquisition or IPO) across all exited Israeli startups. The histogram below shows the distribution of those exit times in 1-year buckets, with the rightmost bucket capturing every exit at 30 or more years.

startups:industry-mix.title: Industry Share Over Time
startups:industry-mix.description: Stacked bar chart of the industry mix of Israeli startups by founding year. Each bar is one year, broken into 6 industry categories (IT and Telecom, Healthcare and Food, Consumer Goods and Services, Energy and Utilities, Financial Services, Media and Entertainment). Sub-industries that fall outside these 6 are bucketed into Unknown and excluded from the visible mix. The legend on the right shows each industry overall total and share across all years.

startups:signal-deeptech.title: Deeptech
startups:signal-deeptech.description: Share of Israeli startups flagged as deeptech. Deep tech companies require significant resources, long development cycles, specialized expertise, and substantial investment. The 10-segment meter visualizes that share. The number on the right is the absolute count of deeptech startups.

startups:signal-global.title: Operating Globally
startups:signal-global.description: Share of Israeli startups that have a product with a global audience. The 10-segment meter visualizes that share. The number on the right is the absolute count of globally operating startups.

startups:trending-up.title: Sub-Industries Trending Up By Share Of Total
startups:trending-up.description: Top 5 sub-industries whose share of new Israeli startups has grown the most over the past 10 founding years. Each line is one sub-industry. The value at year Y is the share of startups founded in year Y whose primary sub-industry falls in that group. The dashed tail marks the most recent year, which is still incomplete.

startups:trending-down.title: Sub-Industries Trending Down By Share Of Total
startups:trending-down.description: Top 5 sub-industries whose share of new Israeli startups has shrunk the most over the past 10 founding years. Each line is one sub-industry. The value at year Y is the share of startups founded in year Y whose primary sub-industry falls in that group. The dashed tail marks the most recent year, which is still incomplete.

startups:feed-funding.title: Funding Feed
startups:feed-funding.description: Latest funding rounds added to the dataset, gathered from multiple verifiable sources. Unlike the headline funding figures, this feed carries every round type, grants and venture debt included, each one flagged with isNonEquity so you can tell them apart.

startups:feed-new-startups.title: New Startups
startups:feed-new-startups.description: Latest startups added to the dataset. Not necessarily new Startups founded.

startups:feed-notable.title: Notable Events
startups:feed-notable.description: Latest notable events gathered form news feeds, including acquisitions, IPOs, corporate events, strategic partnerships and more.

newStartups.description: Software company providing tailored business software solutions, including a warehouse management system for inventory storage and real-time information access, alongside custom software development services
Cloud-based platform for managing employee expenses and petty cash, streamlining expense submission, approval workflows, and reimbursement for businesses.

Decentralized legal-tech platform providing blockchain-based proof of intellectual property ownership, generating court-admissible timestamped copyright records and enabling rights transfer via smart contracts for developers, freelancers and creators.

A developer onboarding platform for blockchain ecosystems that lets contributors browse and filter open GitHub issues to find projects matching their skills, while project maintainers offer custom incentives such as tokens, NFTs and POAPs.

AI-based all-in-one cloud business management platform for small and midsize businesses, combining CRM, project and task management, invoicing, time tracking, document management, e-signatures, surveys, customer messaging and AI-assisted features with local tax and payroll workflows.

Developer security tooling that scans AI-built application repositories for launch and production-readiness risks such as missing row-level security, exposed secret keys, unsigned payment webhooks and environment-variable drift, and hands the fixes to AI coding agents; checks run locally with no account required

Remote MCP server that carries working context between AI tools, storing structured handoffs with task goals, decisions and open items so work can resume in another tool without re-asking settled questions

Cloud service that lets developers and their AI agents hand off containerized GPU workloads such as training, evaluation and batch inference to rented cloud compute, with free cost estimates, hard per-job spending limits and delivery of outputs and run records

Web-based social media management tool that lets users compose a post once and schedule or publish it across multiple social networks, with automated direct-message workflows, a unified inbox for comments and messages, link-in-bio pages, and cross-network analytics
Developer tools company that reduces LLM API costs for coding-agent teams by keeping prompt caches warm, analyzing agent session logs to surface cache-waste costs and optimizing cache-hit rates

Online event-management platform for weddings and celebrations offering digital invitation design, WhatsApp and SMS delivery, real-time RSVP tracking, guest seating management, and phone-based RSVP workflows from a centralized dashboard

Voice AI company building Hebrew-language conversational agents with a native Israeli voice for customer conversations and business workflows, offering a platform for agent creation, telephony, knowledge, integrations, testing and monitoring, plus fully managed design, integration and operation of voice-agent deployments, and a location intelligence tool that maps customer demand for local businesses.

Hebrew-language web-based event management system for weddings and private events, combining guest-list management, RSVP collection via messaging apps and automated phone calls, digital invitations, seating arrangement tools, and credit-card gift collection in a single browser dashboard.

Cloud-based manufacturing execution system for small and mid-size factories, managing work orders, machines, production lines and OEE metrics with real-time visibility for production, shift and quality teams across devices

Test automation platform where AI agents operate browsers, mobile apps and devices, capture interactions with automatic event and state detection, convert analytics into assertions, and replay test flows with AI-based recovery when selectors or timing drift.

AI-powered platform that generates professional landing pages and digital business cards from a one-sentence business description, edited via simple conversational chat and managed from a smartphone, with built-in lead capture and contact sharing for small businesses and self-employed professionals

Cloud-based accounting and bookkeeping software platform that lets businesses manage accounts remotely, track income and expenses, generate reports and digital invoices, and pay tax authorities online with minimal manual work.

SaaS platform for WhatsApp business automation built on the official WhatsApp Cloud API, offering AI chat agents, a visual no-code flow builder, lead management, appointment scheduling, targeted messaging campaigns, and customer surveys for businesses.

AI-powered no-code platform that turns natural-language chat into working Chrome extensions, userscripts, browser automations and data scrapers, letting non-developers customize and automate their browsing experience.

AI-powered marketing platform that plans, creates and optimizes paid and organic campaigns across major ad and social channels, with AI-generated ad copy, images and video, SEO tools, marketing automations and AI visibility tracking for business owners

notable.summary: Yuki launched Yuki Free Cost Analysis, a free Snowflake Native App available on the Snowflake Marketplace with unlimited access, which analyzes a Snowflake account's query and metering history in place and produces a verified cost-savings report (spend profile, warehouse-level savings opportunities, performance metrics, projected annual savings) exportable as a PDF.
A class action lawsuit was filed against Tigo Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: TYGO), as announced by Pomerantz LLP, which is notifying investors of the action.
EcoMoat published an analysis downgrading Nike to a 'Moderate Moat' rating due to declining engagement and increased competition.
Tonic Security published a security advisory (PHP2Shell) detailing affected systems, fixes and mitigations, alongside a related advisory on a LiteLLM supply-chain compromise.

Cygrid exited stealth and launched its identity-enforcement platform, which maps human, non-human and AI agent identities into a single intelligence graph and continuously enforces access limits, blocking risky actions before they execute. At launch the company reported ~20 design partners across fintech, e-commerce and SaaS (including Barfer's and Horizn Studios) and more than 2,000 risky identity actions stopped.

Announced a partnership with Apella WertpapierService GmbH, a liability umbrella for securities distribution partners, to offer a Unified Managed Account solution integrating portagon's private-markets products into Apella's advisory and distribution process; Incore Asset Management Solution AG will integrate portagon's system into its 'MyWebDepot' platform, with integration expected in Q1 2027.

Co-exhibited with Sony Latin America at booth M122 (Mexico Hall) and hosted a free integrator training session, 'Pro BRAVIA & NoviSign - New Opportunities in Digital Signage' (October 22, Education 3 - Petén), at InfoComm América Latina 2026, World Trade Center Mexico City, October 21-23, 2026.

Warp Sciences emerged from stealth, launching a U.S.-based chemistry contract research organization (CRO) that combines expert chemists, AI, and robotics to make and test molecules for drug discovery, with an initial focus on lead optimization analog synthesis. Founded by Kevin Weil (CEO, ex-OpenAI), Sol Reisberg (CSO, ex-Terremoto Biosciences), Mano Paluri (CTO, ex-Meta), and DJ Patil (COO, ex-Devoted Health/White House). Announced alongside $215M in funding led by Lightspeed at an $865M valuation (funding tracked separately).

Tigo Energy announced a manufacturer declaration of compatibility from Fronius International GmbH covering Tigo TS4-A-F, TS4-A-2F, TS4-A-O and TS4-X-O Flex MLPE products with multiple Fronius inverter families (Primo GEN24, Symo GEN24, Verto, Tauro, Tauro ECO), extending manufacturer-confirmed compatibility worldwide including the US and Canada.

Partnered with Smartbird, Inc. (NASDAQ: BIRD) to deliver managed, sovereign-by-design AI infrastructure services, combining WEKA NeuralMesh software with Smartbird's dedicated AI clusters for enterprise AI workloads in regulated industries.

Launched CopilotKit Soar, a self-hosted AI coworker product for companies: forward-deployed engineers set it up on the customer's own servers (single machine to Kubernetes on EKS/AKS/GKE) under the customer's brand, with IT governance (approval checkpoints, SSO/SAML/OIDC, SCIM 2.0, SIEM audit trail), any agent via AG-UI, any MCP server, and any model including local OpenAI-compatible servers. Built on the previously open-sourced OpenBot, OpenMuse, OpenDots and OpenTag projects; available in early access.

Announced its Autumn 2026 Release, led by Genesis agentic AI with expanded device and OS access, on-premises Genesis (expected early 2027), AI-based CDR analysis in Pathfinder, Corellium Falcon Mirror Add-on, next-generation DJI drone forensics (CFID v4), Guardian storage/governance enhancements, and the Cellebrite Tactical Extraction Kit (C-Tek) field kit.

Launched a rebuilt reacheffect.com website and a new unified self-serve dashboard for advertisers, affiliates and publishers, featuring AI-assisted campaign setup (AI Fill), a seven-step campaign flow, reusable filters, budget spreading, an offers wall with 1,200+ CPA offers and smartlinks, and live traffic data across 195 GEOs.
Appointed Ronen Morecki as Chief Operating Officer; he joins from monday.com where he was VP of Payments, and will lead payments strategy and Merchant of Record expansion.
Named winner of three Top InfoSec Innovator Awards for 2026.
Tigo Energy presented at the LD Micro 20th Annual Main Event Conference, outlining a growth plan focused on margins, storage growth and utility software expansion.

Fhenix CoFHE went live on Arbitrum mainnet (partner mainnet, permissioned at launch), bringing encrypted computation and dual-mode confidential tokens to the Arbitrum ecosystem. First design partners Obolos and Alpha Engine launched on day one; the system was audited by Consensys Diligence, and Fhenix also announced work on a confidential stablecoin with Tandem.
Announced collaboration with NVIDIA on advancing agentic AI security, covering security for agentic AI workflows and NVIDIA-based deployments.
Launched Novee Workflows, automating scheduled assessments and tasks beyond the pentest itself.

Launched the Tomorrow.io Terminal in beta — a platform aggregating weather, river and disaster-agency warnings and readings worldwide, organized by impact, place, storm and events, with daily 'The Atmosphere Today' editions, structured pages readable by AI agents, and access via waitlist at terminal.tomorrow.io.
